terminology_test.formography_explanation: Formography systematically maps context-bounded forms through alternative factorizations, typed relations, and source-custodied projections while declaring losses and preserving distinguishability without universal ontology claims. It names and compares forms under bounded questions, preserves factorization alternatives, maintains scoped relation types, tracks source authority and custody explicitly, and declares projection loss visibly.
terminology_test.governed_property_graph_explanation: A governed property graph stores and traverses entities and relations under declared custody, access control, and schema constraints while tracking version, authority, and transformation rules. Property graphs support alternative paths, qualify edges with metadata, and apply governance rules across vertices and edges without requiring a single canonical factorization or declaring all representational loss.
terminology_test.reason: It names the explicit comparison, custody, and loss-declaration practice rather than the storage technology.

overall_assessment.note: The coder judged domain fidelity and loss declaration to exceed typed property-graph storage.
